newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan defence ministry accused of false accounting.
newsitem.headline: Japan defence ministry accused of false accounting.

text.p: Japan's public spending watchdog has accused the defence ministry of falsifying budget documents regarding shipment of equipment for navy warships, a spokesman for a firm involved in the transaction said on Wednesday.

The Board of Audit, an independent body which audits government accounts, found falsified documents prepared by trading house Marubeni Corp on behalf of the ministry, which is formally known as the Defence Agency, a spokesman for Marubeni said.
Board of Audit and defence ministry spokesmen refused to comment on the case, which was first reported by the Mainichi Shimbun newspaper on Wednesday.
The charges stem from documents related to 14 shipboard tractors sent to the United States for an overhaul in February 1995, the daily said.

The defence ministry asked Marubeni to falsify records so it looked like the shipment took place in May 1995, because there was a budget shortfall for the April 1994-March 1995 fiscal year, according to the daily.
A Marubeni spokesman said that his company was involved in falsifying the official documents at the request of the defence ministry.

"They (Marubeni officials involved in the case) accepted the request because they were told by the agency that it was needed to receive payments for conventional deals. It's a one-off case but it was careless," the Marubeni spokesman said.
